summary: Checked 2026-09-13 against primary sources (PyPI JSON API, GitHub REST API and raw source, Crossref, bioRxiv API, readthedocs) plus real pip installs in scratch venvs on CPython 3.12.10 / Windows 11. SciUnit: latest version is 0.2.8 (GitHub release 2023-12-19; PyPI sdist uploaded 2024-01-03), MIT license (LICENSE file), requires_python >=3.7. Last commit to master was 2023-12-26. CI only tests Python 3.7-3.10 on ubuntu-latest. It installs on Python 3.12 (sdist only) and a small Test/Capability/Model/ZScore/TestSuite test ran correctly, so it is usable but low-activity. An open PR from 2026-02-19 proposes modernising packaging and the CI matrix. NeuronUnit is effectively unmaintained and not usable on Python 3.12 as a dependency. PyPI's latest is 0.1.8.2 (2016-07-04): it installs, but neuronunit.models fails to import because pyneuroml is not declared as a dependency. The GitHub default branch (dev, last commit 2021-04-22; newest branch activity 2021-07-18) declares version 0.19 and pins old packages (pandas==1.1.0, scikit_learn==0.23.2, allensdk==0.16.3, lxml==4.4.1, neo==0.5.2). It also pulls a git+ssh BluePyOpt fork, so pip install from git fails. Its requirements.txt and tests/fi.py contain unresolved git merge-conflict markers (SyntaxError on import). Its models/backends import TemporaryDirectory from sciunit.utils, which does not exist in sciunit 0.2.8. The repo has no LICENSE file; the GitHub license API returns 404 and only setup.cfg/PyPI metadata declare MIT. NeuronUnit does contain relevant prior art: a jNeuroML backend that runs LEMS files through pyNeuroML, square-pulse and arbitrary-waveform current capabilities, and tests for rheobase (binary search), input resistance, membrane time constant, capacitance, resting potential, AP width/amplitude/threshold, ISI/CV/local variation, FI/firing-rate type, burstiness and Druckmann-2013 AP features. Both tools score a model's predictions against experimental observations (Z, ratio, boolean scores). Neither provides mutation generation, numerically calibrated tolerances for reference-vs-transformed differences, a perturbation-fingerprint detection matrix, protocol-battery selection or held-out evaluation. Recommendation: do not depend on NeuronUnit. Do not make SciUnit a core dependency; borrow its design concepts and cite both. At most, offer SciUnit as an optional export adapter, subject to Neel's decision.

Observed on Windows 11 + CPython 3.12.10: (1) pip install sciunit==0.2.8 succeeds in a short-path venv (pip check clean; resolved numpy 2.5.3, pandas 3.0.5, quantities 0.16.4, ipykernel 7.3.0, ipython 9.17.1), and a Test/Model/Capability/ZScore judge plus TestSuite judge ran. (2) In a venv under a deep path, the install failed with an OSError on a vendored debugpy file because Windows long-path support is not enabled; this is environment-specific, not a sciunit defect, but it matters for NeuroSem setup instructions. (3) pip install neuronunit==0.1.8.2 succeeds; neuronunit.tests imports, neuronunit.models fails (no pyneuroml). (4) pip install from GitHub dev fails (git+ssh BluePyOpt: host key verification failed). Installed with --no-deps plus unpinned modern deps, only neuronunit.capabilities, tests.passive and tests.waveform import; tests package, fi, dynamics, druckmann2013, channel fail with SyntaxError (merge-conflict marker in fi.py line 199); models, backends and lems fail with ImportError (TemporaryDirectory missing from sciunit.utils 0.2.8).

reuse_for_neurosem: Cite SciUnit (Omar, Aldrich, Gerkin 2014, ICSE Companion, DOI 10.1145/2591062.2591129) and NeuronUnit (Gerkin et al. 2019 bioRxiv preprint, DOI 10.1101/665331, no journal version recorded by bioRxiv) as the closest prior frameworks for executable, data-driven neuron-model validation tests.
Borrow SciUnit's capability-based test/model contract: protocols declare required model capabilities and unsupported combinations produce an explicit 'not applicable' status, never a silent pass.
Borrow the ProtocolToFeaturesTest decomposition (setup_protocol -> run -> extract_features) as the internal structure of a NeuroSem protocol, implemented natively.

Borrow SciUnit's explicit incomplete/error score vocabulary (ErrorScore, NoneScore, InsufficientDataScore) to encode undefined eFEL features and simulation failures distinctly, consistent with the handoff rule never to substitute zero.
Use TestM2M/ScoreMatrixM2M as the prior-art comparison point for reference-vs-transformed comparisons, and optionally as an export format.

Use NeuronUnit's stimulus capability vocabulary (square pulse with amplitude/delay/duration; arbitrary waveform via neo AnalogSignal) as a reference when designing NeuroSem's protocol manifest schema.

Use NeuronUnit's rheobase binary search, passive-property (input resistance, time constant, capacitance, resting potential) and AP waveform test definitions as independent cross-checks for NeuroSem/eFEL feature definitions during development. Do not import them.

Record NeuronUnit's existing rheobase, FI, ISI, burstiness and Druckmann-2013 feature tests in docs/novelty_matrix.csv so NeuroSem does not claim novelty for rheobase search, multi-feature characterisation or feature-based model scoring.
If Neel wants interoperability, add an optional (non-core, extras) adapter exporting NeuroSem fingerprints as SciUnit scores, pinned to sciunit==0.2.8 after a Python 3.12 CI check. Decision required.
not_provided_new_for_neurosem: Controlled single-fault mutation operators for NeuroML/LEMS (stimulus, biophysical, reference, numerical families), one-change enforcement and mutant provenance: not found in SciUnit or NeuronUnit.
Classification of mutants as structurally invalid, non-executable, numerically unstable, behaviourally equivalent, non-equivalent or silent under canonical testing.

Differential reference-vs-transformed regression with feature-specific tolerances calibrated by numerical refinement (h, h/2, h/4) and frozen before held-out testing. SciUnit scores compare predictions to observations (Z, ratio, relative difference with a user-set scale), with no convergence-based calibration.
Perturbation fingerprint (feature vector across a protocol battery) and binary mutant-by-protocol detection matrix with per-detection evidence (protocol, feature, threshold, trace).
Greedy maximum-coverage protocol-battery selection, plus count-matched and runtime-matched random baselines and detection-versus-cost curves.
Held-out model and held-out mutation-family splits, leakage barriers, hashed split manifests and held-out access logging.
Valid-transformation false-positive control (unit conversion, renames, reordering, formatting) and the no-change control.

Rheobase-normalised protocol battery beyond square pulses: ramp, hyperpolarisation-release rebound, paired pulses and deterministic chirp. NeuronUnit only exposes square-current and generic arbitrary-waveform capabilities; no such protocol classes were found in the test modules examined.
Run-level provenance (model/file hashes, simulator version, dt, seed, environment digest, Git commit) with immutable raw results; SciUnit's backend cache is not a provenance system.
A maintained, Python 3.12-compatible jNeuroML/LEMS execution adapter: NeuronUnit's does not import today, so NeuroSem must build its own thin adapter on pyNeuroML.
Integration of eFEL as the frozen feature extractor with recorded settings (NeuronUnit dev lists efel in install_requires, but no efel usage was found in the modules downloaded here).
handoff_assumption_issues: OUTDATED: the handoff's 'Reuse rather than rebuild' list includes 'SciUnit/NeuronUnit: scientific model testing'. NeuronUnit cannot be reused as a dependency today. Its last PyPI release is from 2016 (models import fails without undeclared pyneuroml). Its GitHub dev branch (last commit 2021) has merge-conflict markers in fi.py and requirements.txt, a git+ssh-only BluePyOpt dependency, legacy pins incompatible with Python 3.12, and an API mismatch with sciunit 0.2.8 (TemporaryDirectory). NeuronUnit should move from 'reuse' to 'cite / borrow concepts'.

UNCERTAIN LICENSE: the neuronunit repository has no LICENSE file (GitHub license API 404); MIT appears only in setup.cfg and PyPI metadata. Copying NeuronUnit code into NeuroSem would need license clarification; citing and reimplementing does not.

SCIENTIFICALLY DIFFERENT PURPOSE: SciUnit/NeuronUnit validate a model's predictions against experimental observations (Z, ratio, boolean scores against observation mean/std). NeuroSem needs behavioural-preservation testing between a reference model and a transformed model, with numerically calibrated tolerances. Reuse is conceptual rather than functional; TestM2M is the closest built-in construct.

MAINTENANCE RISK FOR SCIUNIT: sciunit is installable on Python 3.12 but its last release is v0.2.8 (Dec 2023), its CI tests only Python 3.7-3.10 on Linux, and it pulls a heavy Jupyter stack (ipykernel, nbconvert, ipython). A core dependency would add fragility to a frozen, Dockerised research environment. The PR modernising packaging (#226, 2026-02-19) is unmerged.

NOVELTY BOUNDARY CONFIRMED: NeuronUnit already implements rheobase search, input resistance, membrane time constant, capacitance, resting potential, AP width/amplitude/threshold, ISI/CV, burstiness, FI and Druckmann-2013 features. This supports the handoff's instruction not to claim novelty for feature extraction or multi-protocol characterisation. Rheobase search must be listed as existing prior art.

SETUP RISK (Windows): sciunit's dependency tree includes files whose install paths exceed Windows MAX_PATH in deep directories; pip failed until a shorter venv path was used. Setup commands should use short paths, Docker, or note long-path support.

EXECUTION DEPENDENCY: NeuronUnit's (and generally pyNeuroML's) jNeuroML route requires a Java runtime; Java was absent on this machine. The pyNeuroML/jNeuroML audit must confirm how Java is provided for the 'jNeuroML only' pilot.
STALE DOCUMENTATION HOSTS: the metadata homepages sciunit.scidash.org and neuronunit.scidash.org did not resolve; the readthedocs sites should be cited as documentation URLs instead.
uncertainties: Whether a maintained fork or successor of NeuronUnit exists outside scidash/neuronunit and russelljjarvis/neuronunit (last pushed 2021-12-18) was not exhaustively searched; GitHub code/repo search was not used to save API quota.
NeuronUnit tests were checked for importability only; no NeuronUnit test was executed against a real LEMS model (no Java runtime; models/backends fail to import).
Whether sciunit 0.2.8 behaves correctly beyond the smoke test (notebook utilities, disk cache, TestM2M scoring) on Python 3.12, NumPy 2.5 and pandas 3.0 was not tested.
The status of NeuronUnit's master and prime branches (e.g. whether prime installs more cleanly than dev) was not install-tested; only dev (default branch) and PyPI 0.1.8.2 were.
How NeuronUnit uses efel (listed in dev install_requires) was not determined; only a subset of modules was downloaded and none referenced efel.
The content of the 2014 ICSE Companion paper, the 2019 NeuronUnit preprint and the 2018 Phil Trans B paper was not read in full; only bibliographic metadata and the bioRxiv abstract were retrieved.
DBLP blocked automated API access (bot-check page) and OpenAlex returned 'Rate limit exceeded' on a second query; bibliographic facts rely on Crossref and the bioRxiv API.
Documentation landing-page facts (readthedocs) came from a fetch-model summary rather than raw HTML inspection.
